coverage_override.reason: The hand summon effect, summon search/banish trigger, delayed return trigger, and shared each-effect HOPT are four audit units.

effects.printed_clause: Banish 1 Fish from your hand or field; Special Summon this card from your hand.
effects.lua_implementation: The hand Ignition Effect searches an eligible Fish in hand/MZONE with e:GetHandler() passed as the exception card in both existence and selection calls, verifies removing the selected card opens a zone when necessary, banishes it as cost, then summons the still-related handler.

official_references.matched_structure: Uses a hand effect with a separate card cost followed by self-Special Summoning.
Banishes a Fish-related card as cost and resolves a Special Summon.

effects.review_note: Rejected the reported self-cost defect: e:GetHandler() is already supplied as the exception argument to both Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard and Duel.SelectMatchingCard.

effects.printed_clause: If Normal or Special Summoned: add to hand or banish 1 Level 4 or lower Ghoti monster from your Deck.
effects.lua_implementation: Normal/Special trigger clones select one eligible low-Level Ghoti from Deck and offer the legal add or face-up banish operation under a shared hard limit.

official_references.matched_structure: Uses Ghoti summon-event and banishment/search processing under a hard once-per-turn.

effects.printed_clause: During the Standby Phase of the next turn after this card was banished: Special Summon this banished card.
effects.lua_implementation: EVENT_REMOVE records the banish turn; a banished-zone Standby trigger requires a later turn and retained flag, then Special Summons the related card when a zone is available.

official_references.matched_structure: Records banishment and returns the Ghoti during a later Standby Phase.
Uses banished-zone delayed phase triggering and Special Summon legality.

effects.printed_clause: You can only use each effect of Shekup, Sting of the Ghoti once per turn.
effects.lua_implementation: The three activated effects use id, id+100, and id+200 hard count keys.

official_references.matched_structure: Uses distinct id-derived hard once-per-turn keys for Ghoti effects.
